You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H7521

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "Be pleased with, delight in; accept favorably; be accepted; enjoy/pay off sabbaths; be favored; seek favor"
  Readable gloss: "A verb expressing the full arc of divine and human favor — from inward delight to outward acceptance. In its Qal active form ratsah describes God taking pleasure in a person's ways (1 Chr 29:17) or a worshiper's offering (Mal 1:8). The Nifal passive conveys the state of being found acceptable, a critical concept in Levitical sacrifice law: will this offering 'be accepted' on the offerer's behalf (Lev 1:4)? A remarkable specialized usage appears in the sabbatical-year theology of Lev 26:34-43, where the desolate land finally 'enjoys' its missed sabbaths during exile. The passive participle yields the adjective 'favored,' applied to Asher's tribal blessing (Deut 33:24) and to Mordecai's standing among his people (Esth 10:3)."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "Qal: be pleased with, delight in"
    Enriched: The core Qal sense: to be pleased with, take delight in. Arabic radiya ('be well-pleased'), Korean gippuhada ('rejoice, delight'), and Swahili -pendezwa ('be delighted') all converge here. Gen 33:10 records Jacob's relief that Esau has 'been pleased' with him; 1 Chr 28:4 celebrates God's choice of Judah and David as acts of divine pleasure.
    Existing Spanish translations: Cuando-agradan, Qué-te-agrade, Se-complace, Te-complaciste, a-favorecer, aprobó, desean, disfrute, en-su-deleitarse, que-se-complace, se-agradó, se-complace, te-complaciste-en-ellos, y-aceptaste-me, y-corriste, y-los-agradarás, y-me-complaceré-en, ¿Te-aceptará?
  Sense 2: "Qal: accept favorably"
    Enriched: Transitive Qal: to accept favorably — the act of receiving offerings, persons, or prayers with approval. Korean batda ('receive') and Arabic qabila ('accept') highlight the reception-event. Lev 26:41 warns that the land will not accept them until they humble themselves; 2 Sam 24:23 expresses Araunah's hope that God will accept David's offering.
    Existing Spanish translations: acepta, aceptaré, los-acepta, los-aceptaré, los-acepto, los-aceptó, os-aceptaré, pagarán, te-acepte, y-lo-acepta, y-os-aceptaré, ¿Aceptaré
  Sense 3: "Nifal: be accepted, be acceptable"
    Enriched: Nifal passive: to be accepted, be found acceptable — the sacrificial-technical sense governing whether an offering meets the required standard. Lev 1:4 stipulates that a burnt offering 'shall be accepted' on behalf of the worshiper. Korean badadeul-yojirira ('will be accepted') and Swahili -kubaliwa confirm the passive-stative reading across languages.
    Existing Spanish translations: perdonada-es, será-aceptado, serán-aceptados, y-será-aceptado
  Sense 4: "Qal/Hifil: enjoy, pay off (sabbaths)"
    Enriched: A specialized theological usage: the land 'enjoying' or 'paying off' its missed sabbath years during exile (Lev 26:34, 43; 2 Chr 36:21). Spanish disfrutó ('enjoyed') and pagará ('will pay off') reveal the dual nuance — both compensatory rest and debt-settlement. This sense is unique to the sabbatical-year legislation and its Chronicler echo.
    Existing Spanish translations: disfrutó, pagará, y-pagará
  Sense 5: "Qal pass. ptcp: favored, acceptable"
    Enriched: Qal passive participle functioning as an adjective: favored, acceptable, well-regarded. Deut 33:24 blesses Asher as 'favored among his brothers'; Esth 10:3 describes Mordecai as 'accepted by the multitude of his brethren.' Arabic mardiyyan ('approved') and Korean eunhye-reul banneun ('receiving favor') confirm the adjectival participial force.
    Existing Spanish translations: el-favorito-de, y-aceptado
  Sense 6: ""
    Enriched: In Job 20:10 the verb takes on the nuance of seeking or currying favor — the wicked man's children 'seek favor from the poor' they exploited. English 'seek favor from' and Spanish buscarán favor de capture the desperate, supplicatory reversal of fortune Zophar describes.
    Existing Spanish translations: buscarán-favor-de
  Sense 7: ""
    Enriched: In 1 Sam 29:4 the Philistine commanders ask how David might 'reconcile himself' with Saul — using ratsah for the political act of regaining an overlord's favor through betrayal on the battlefield. English 'reconcile himself' and Spanish se reconciliará point to an interpersonal-political dimension distinct from cultic acceptance.
    Existing Spanish translations: se-reconciliará
